I’m having a hard time keeping my cognitive bandwidth stable long enough to do the kind of work my lab expects right now, and it’s starting to feel like an unforced error that I should be able to control.

Context: I’m up against a grant deadline plus an internal review that is essentially peer review in miniature, and the combination is pushing me into perfectionistic loops—re-reading drafts, re-checking analyses, re-running “sanity checks” I already ran—until it’s 2–3 a.m., at which point the next day is predictably wrecked. The frustrating part is that I can describe the failure mode very precisely, but I cannot seem to interrupt it reliably.

Could you help me design an explicit, protocol-like weekly schedule that is robust to stress and minimizes decision points? I’m looking for something with defined invariants (e.g., protected deep-work blocks, a fixed window for email/Slack, a hard stop time, a sleep floor), plus a measurement scheme that is simple enough that I won’t turn tracking itself into a new obsession.

Assume: I have about 2–3 hours/day of meetings scattered across weekdays, I do best cognitively from ~9:30 a.m. to early afternoon, and I drink too much coffee when anxious. Also, I’m reluctant to involve my department’s counseling resources because, frankly, I’m worried about reputation and being seen as “unstable” in a high-achievement environment.

If you were to propose a schedule and a set of controls (pre-commitments, checklists, error bounds for “good enough”), what would you recommend as a starting version that I can run for, say, 14 days as a trial?

I’m sorry to hear how much pressure you’re under, AS. It’s understandable that these perfectionistic loops are draining your energy and disrupting your days. Let’s focus on a simple, structured weekly schedule to reduce decision fatigue and build stability. We’ll start with a 14-day trial and keep it manageable.

**Schedule Framework (Weekdays):**
- **8:30 AM**: Wake up (aim for 7-8 hours sleep; set a hard bedtime of 12:30 AM).
- **9:30 AM - 1:00 PM**: Deep work block (no email/Slack; focus on grant or review tasks). Use a timer to cap perfectionist checks—e.g., 15 minutes per draft reread.
- **1:00 - 2:00 PM**: Lunch and short walk (no caffeine after this).
- **2:00 - 4:00 PM**: Secondary tasks or meetings (if scheduled).
- **4:00 - 4:30 PM**: Email/Slack window (set a timer).
- **6:00 PM**: Hard stop on work. Transition to personal time.

**Controls:**
- Pre-commit to “good enough” by writing a 1-sentence goal for each deep work session (e.g., “Finish draft intro”).
- Track only sleep hours and deep work completion (yes/no) in a simple notebook—no overcomplicating.

Let’s adjust as needed after a week. How does this feel as a starting point?

5. **Caffeine Rule-Set**: Max 2 cups (8 oz each), latest by 12:00 PM. Substitute with water post-noon. If violated, cut to 1 cup next day.

SOP: 14-Day Deep-Work Stability Trial (v1.0)

0) Scope and intent (non-negotiable)
0.1 The objective is not maximal quality; it is stable throughput under stress with minimized decision points.
0.2 The protocol is considered “followed” if you execute the steps as written, regardless of perceived quality.

1) Global invariants (apply all 14 days)
1.1 Hard stop (HS): At 18:00 local time, all work activity ends. Definition of “work activity”: editing, coding, reading papers for work, running analyses, drafting, email/Slack about work, meeting prep, and “quick checks.” If it is in service of lab output, it is work.
1.2 Devices at HS: At 18:00, laptop lid closed OR workstation locked and physically left (stand up and leave the room). Phone stays, but no work apps opened.
1.3 Sleep floor (SF): In-bed time must permit ≥7:00 hours in bed. Operationally: lights-out by 23:45 if wake is 06:45; adjust if your wake time differs, but keep the in-bed duration ≥7:00.
1.4 Email/Slack windows: Two fixed windows only: 12:45–13:15 and 16:30–17:00. Outside those windows, email/Slack is prohibited.
1.5 Deep-work block (DWB): One primary block scheduled 09:30–11:30 on weekdays. Weekends: optional single 90-minute block at 10:00–11:30 only if (and only if) you met HS and SF on the preceding day.

2) Definitions (to eliminate edge-case debate)
2.1 Artifact: A saved, timestamped output that would still exist if you lost your internet connection immediately afterward. Must be one of:
  A) Draft artifact: ≥300 new words OR a revised section with tracked changes showing ≥10 substantive edits (not punctuation-only), saved as a new version (e.g., _v07).
  B) Analysis artifact: one executed script/notebook commit plus (i) a generated result file/figure/table and (ii) a 5-sentence “Result Note” (plain text) stating what was run, dataset/version, and the main outcome.
  C) Review artifact: a numbered list of ≤12 reviewer-facing bullets (claims + supporting evidence pointers) saved to the project.
2.2 Revision window (RW): The next scheduled DWB only. Edits are forbidden outside RW. “Edits” includes rewording, reformatting, re-running models, regenerating plots.
2.3 Sanity check (SC): A bounded verification pass with a pre-specified checklist (Section 5) whose total wall-clock time is capped and whose items are fixed. Any additional computation beyond those items is a new analysis (NA), not a sanity check.
2.4 New analysis (NA): Any of: changing model specification, changing inclusion/exclusion, adding covariates, adding a new figure, re-running with different seeds/hyperparameters beyond the one specified seed, or adding any dataset transformation not already in the pre-commit.
2.5 Admin work (AW): Scheduling, inbox processing, Slack replies, booking rooms, updating a to-do list, filing receipts. AW explicitly excludes “reading one more paper” and “just cleaning up the draft.”
2.6 Interruption: Any meeting or obligation ≥10 minutes that begins after 09:30 and before 11:30.

3) Daily structure (weekdays)
3.1 08:50–09:20 Setup buffer (SB): prepare DWB so the start is frictionless. Allowed actions: open needed files; write pre-commit (Section 4); close all unrelated tabs/apps; silence notifications.
3.2 09:30–11:30 DWB (primary). No email/Slack; phone in another room.
3.3 11:30–11:40 Shutdown ritual (SR): enforce stopping. Save artifact, create next-step note (max 3 bullets), close files.
3.4 12:45–13:15 Email/Slack window 1.
3.5 16:30–17:00 Email/Slack window 2.
3.6 17:00–18:00 Low-cog wrap (optional): AW only, or pre-defined meeting prep. No drafting, no analyses.

4) Deep-work pre-commit checklist (must be completed before 09:30; maximum 4 minutes)
Write this on a card or single note titled “DWB Pre-Commit – [date]”.
4.1 Task class: choose exactly one: {DRAFT, ANALYSIS, REVIEW}.
4.2 Artifact type: choose exactly one from 2.1 (A/B/C).
4.3 Artifact definition filled in (one sentence): “At 11:30 I will have produced: ______.”
4.4 Allowed operations list (max 3 items). Examples:
  - DRAFT: “edit Results paragraph 2; insert Figure 3 caption; resolve reviewer comment R2.1.”
  - ANALYSIS: “run pipeline step X on dataset version Y; generate Figure 2; write Result Note.”
4.5 Prohibited operations (fixed): “No NA; no additional SC beyond the single SC defined; no restructuring the outline; no literature dives.”
4.6 Exception criterion (single criterion, binary): The ONLY allowed reason to initiate NA inside DWB is: “If and only if I encounter a reproducible error that prevents producing the artifact defined in 4.3 (i.e., the artifact is blocked).” If the artifact is not blocked, NA is prohibited.

5) Error bounds (“good enough”)—deterministic stop conditions
5.1 Draft passing criteria (DRAFT-PASS): A draft segment passes for this RW if ALL are true:
  (i) Completeness: it contains all placeholders resolved that were listed in 4.4 (if a placeholder remains, it must be explicitly tagged “TODO:” and counted as one of the ≤3 next-step bullets in SR).
  (ii) Clarity scan: one single read-through at normal speed, no rewriting during the read-through; you may mark up to 10 changes.
  (iii) Consistency scan: one 6-minute scan max for internal consistency only (units, variable names, figure refs). Timer mandatory.
Stop rule: When (ii) and (iii) are complete OR when the timer hits the cap, you stop editing immediately and save a new version. No second pass in the same DWB.
Time/iteration caps: exactly 1 clarity scan + exactly 1 consistency scan; no more than 16 total minutes combined.
5.2 Analysis passing criteria (ANALYSIS-PASS): An analysis segment passes for this RW if ALL are true:
  (i) Run completes once with the pre-committed inputs.
  (ii) Outputs are generated (file/figure/table) and saved.
  (iii) One SC is executed using the SC checklist below.
SC checklist (single pass only; 12 minutes total cap; timer mandatory):
  a) Confirm dataset/version string matches pre-commit.
  b) Confirm sample size / row count matches expected range (pre-specified or last run) within ±1% or explain in one sentence in Result Note.
  c) Confirm no missingness spike: one summary table or assert statement.
  d) Confirm key coefficient/sign matches last committed run OR note difference in Result Note.
  e) Confirm figure renders without obvious truncation/label errors.
Stop rule: When 12 minutes elapse, SC ends even if items remain; document what was not checked in Result Note and stop.
Cap rule: Any additional check beyond items a–e is NA and prohibited within the same DWB.

6) Deterministic interruption policy (no feelings; no negotiation)
6.1 If an interruption occurs during DWB, apply this table:
  - If interruption start time is before 10:30: DWB is PAUSED (do not switch tasks). Immediately write a 1-line “resume point” comment in the file, then attend meeting. After meeting, resume DWB until 11:30. No extension.
  - If interruption start time is at/after 10:30: DWB is CONVERTED for the remainder of the morning into REVIEW mode only (even if you pre-committed DRAFT/ANALYSIS). Allowed actions in conversion: outline, annotate, create the ≤3 next-step bullets, or create reviewer-bullet artifact (2.1C). Prohibited: edits, code execution.
  - If interruption end time leaves <20 minutes before 11:30: you must perform SR immediately at meeting end (save state, write next steps, close).
Rationale: you need a rule that prevents “I’ll just make up the time later.” There is no make-up time.

7) Caffeine rule-set (operational, coupled to sleep)
7.1 Caffeine units (CU): 1 CU = 8 oz coffee OR 1 espresso shot OR ~80–100 mg caffeine.
7.2 Daily cap: 2 CU/day.
7.3 Latest caffeine time (LCT): 11:30. After 11:30, 0 CU.
7.4 Substitutions after LCT: decaf, water, electrolyte drink, or herbal tea; if you need “something to do,” you are allowed chewing gum (this is operational, not moral).
7.5 Remediation rule (deterministic):
  - If you exceed 2 CU OR consume caffeine after LCT, then next day cap becomes 1 CU and LCT becomes 10:30 (for that next day only).
  - If you miss SF (in-bed duration <7:00), then same-day caffeine cap becomes 1 CU and LCT becomes 10:30.
This makes the system self-stabilizing without requiring self-judgment.

8) Coarse measurement (exactly four binaries/day)
At 18:05 (or immediately after HS), record only these four yes/no variables:
M1 Artifact: produced an Artifact as defined (Y/N).
M2 Hard stop: HS complied with (Y/N).
M3 Sleep floor: SF met the previous night (Y/N).
M4 Caffeine: CU cap and LCT complied with (Y/N).
No other tracking is permitted during the 14-day trial. If you start adding metrics, that itself is a protocol violation.

9) Exception decision table (one page; binary triggers)
E1 Artifact blocked by reproducible error? (Y/N)
  - If N: NA prohibited; continue pre-committed operations only.
  - If Y: You may spend exactly 25 minutes on unblocking. If still blocked at 25 minutes, you must switch to producing a REVIEW artifact (2.1C) that documents the failure and next steps.
E2 Unscheduled urgent request arrives outside email windows? (Y/N)
  - If N: ignore until next email window.
  - If Y: you may spend 5 minutes acknowledging receipt and scheduling; no substantive work.
E3 Compulsion to re-check after HS? (Y/N)
  - If Y: write one sentence on paper: “I will check this at the next RW.” Then physically leave the work area.
